govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GarrisonJimPlay:
Playboy magazine sat New Orleans District Attorney Jim Garrison down for one of its candid interviews. Garrison laid out his Kennedy assassination investigation for a mass audience. In the course of it he named Clay Shaw and David Ferrie, the two New Orleans men at the center of his case.

The Playboy interview format let public figures talk at length and without a script. For Garrison, it was a chance to take his charges past the courtroom and the evening news. The interview preserves his case in his own voice, as millions of magazine readers first encountered it.

william-auvergne-de-universo:

letters-of-george-borrow-to-the-british-: The private correspondence of George Borrow, the eccentric Victorian traveler and author of Lavengro, written to his employers at the Bible Society. Posted from Spain, Russia, and Portugal in the 1830s, the letters report on his mission to distribute scriptures while doubling as vivid travel writing. They show Borrow the linguist, adventurer, and keen observer in his own unguarded voice.
orlando-furioso: Lodovico Ariosto's great Renaissance epic, first published in 1516, follows the knights of Charlemagne through love, madness, and war. The hero Orlando goes mad with love for the princess Angelica, while the warrior-maiden Bradamante fights her way through enchantments to found a dynasty. Witty, romantic, and wildly inventive, it is one of the supreme poems of Italian literature.
